audit.why: This is the one matchup in my slice where the content chart is well calibrated, and the full layer still contradicts it. That is useful evidence about which layer is at fault file-wide: full.phases[].side is [Skill, Zac, Zac, Skill, Skill, Zac, Zac] in this matchup, and it is the identical sequence in zac__aatrox, zac__ambessa and zac__aurora. It is a default template, not a judgement, and it happens to be applied to matchups Zac wins 50%, 51%, 52% and 53% of the time.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.spikes[0].text calls it 'Feral Scream (E)'. Feral Scream is Cho'Gath's W. His E is Vorpal Spikes, which the same matchup names correctly in content.early and content.whys[3].
audit.why: A wrong slot letter is worse than no slot letter: a player scanning for the silence will watch the wrong key. The matchup gets every other name right, which makes this one stand out as a transcription slip rather than a systemic gap.
audit.corrected: Corrected to Feral Scream (W) and attached its real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.spikes[1].text says 'your P blob revive doesn't help if the sheep-portion body gets Feasted' and content.late says the same via 'even through your P revive if the main body gets eaten'. 'Sheep-portion body' is not a thing in either champion's kit.
audit.why: 'Sheep' is template bleed — it is Lulu's Whimsy, not anything Cho'Gath does. Riot's text for Feast is 'Devours an enemy unit, dealing a high amount of true damage. If the target is killed, Cho'Gath grows, gaining maximum Health.' There is no polymorph, no separate body, and nothing in the description that interacts with a revive. The underlying claim — that Feast defeats Cell Division — may or may not be true, but it cannot be established from the kit files and chogath.json needsResearch is empty, so asserting it either way would be a guess about the single most consequential mechanic in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Removed the garbled claim from both strings and replaced it with what is verified: Feast is true damage, 80s at rank 1, and only 175 range. Did not substitute a denial — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream's silence is mentioned three times as a generic 'silence' and never once connected to what it silences.
audit.why: Zac's escape, his engage and his ultimate are all abilities. A silence does not merely interrupt a combo, it removes Elastic Slingshot from the fight entirely — and Elastic Slingshot is a 21s cooldown at rank 1 against a silence that is 11s at rank 1. Feral Scream is also only 300 range, so it is avoidable by spacing, which is the counterplay nobody stated. dontsFull[1] is literally titled 'Get silenced mid-combo' and its body text is about spending a cooldown for tiny value.
audit.corrected: Connected the silence to Elastic Slingshot specifically in dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[1].d, spikes[0].text, wants.you[2] and breakdown.cooldowns, with the 11s cooldown and 300 range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json W cd 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, range 300, silence flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer names Rupture as the matchup-defining cooldown and builds nine strings around tracking it — 'Engage only on Rupture's cooldown', 'Dive with your jungler when Rupture is down', 'Only take the trade when Cho'Gath's Rupture is down', 'Commit on Rupture's cooldown'. content.early repeats it: 'trade only when his Q is down'. Rupture is a flat 6 second cooldown at every rank.
audit.why: A 6 second cooldown is never meaningfully down. Building the entire commit-timing framework on waiting it out gives the player a window that does not exist, and it displaces the two cooldowns that ARE worth tracking: Feral Scream at 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, which is what actually turns Zac's kit off, and Feast at 80/70/60s. The guide's own dosFull[0].d already has the right instinct — 'Telegraphed. Dodge it.' — and then contradicts itself in the next sentence with 'Only engage once it is down'.
audit.corrected: Reframed the cooldown breakdown around Feral Scream and Feast, and rewrote the strings that told the player to wait out a 6 second ability so they say to dodge the telegraph instead.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json Q cooldown '6', W cd 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, R cd 80/70/60

audit.whatIsWrong: content.whys[0] says 'your Q range trades with his zoning Rupture', implying parity of reach.
audit.why: Rupture is 950 range and Stretching Strikes is 800. He out-ranges Zac's only ranged tool by 150 units, which is why the farm-and-poke stalemate is one Zac loses if he plays it as a poke war. The row's verdict of Skill is right; the reason given is not.
audit.corrected: Gave both numbers and pointed the row at dodging the telegraph rather than at range parity.

audit.whatIsWrong: _missing-interactions.json flags resistances-invalidated for this pairing — 'Cho'Gath bypasses stacking resistances (Feast (R)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here' — and report[8].t recommends Spirit Visage, Thornmail and Plated Steelcaps with no mention of it.
audit.why: Feast is true damage. Every resistance item in the recommended build does literally nothing against the ability the matchup says decides the game, and the only stat that helps is raw maximum health. content.wants.you[1] already says 'Keep HP above Feast (R) execute range', so half the insight is present in the content layer and entirely absent from the build advice it should be driving.
audit.corrected: Added the true-damage consequence to report[8].t, content.late, whys[4] and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four Do/Don't descriptions do not answer their titles. dosFull[1] 'Dodge his Q + W' carries the E-engage trade line. dosFull[2] 'E-knock him up' carries 'Cho'Gath wastes Rupture (Knockup) — commit the full pattern immediately'. dontsFull[1] 'Get silenced mid-combo' carries 'Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown'. dontsFull[2] 'Let him free-stack R' carries the blob-stomping line.
audit.why: Same pasted-description bug as the rest of the slice. dontsFull[2] is the costliest: 'Let him free-stack R' is the only place the guide could explain that Feast grows Cho'Gath's maximum health on every kill, and it explains blob pickups instead.
audit.corrected: Rewrote all four to answer their own headings, and used dontsFull[2].d for the permanent max-health growth.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t all claim stomped blobs cost 'your passive revive margin'.
audit.why: Cell Division's shed chunks are sustain and destructible; the four bloblets appear only on fatal damage and set the revive. Stomping chunks costs sustain only. Getting this right matters more here than anywhere else in the slice, because this matchup separately makes an unverified claim about Feast defeating the revive — the file should at least be internally precise about which half of Cell Division it means.
audit.corrected: Separated the two halves and stated the 5 minute cooldown.

notes: FALSE POSITIVE in the packet: suspectNames flags 'Let's Bounce' in spikes[3].text at distance 1 from 'let's bounce!'. The text on disk actually reads 'use R Let's Bounce! to peel', exclamation mark included, so the name is already correct and the detector appears to be stripping trailing punctuation from one side of the comparison only. No name change made. Deliberately NOT resolved: whether Feast defeats Cell Division's revive. Both content.spikes[1].text and content.late currently assert it does, via the garbled 'sheep-portion body' and 'main body' phrasings, and 'sheep' is unmistakably template bleed from a Lulu matchup rather than anything in Cho'Gath's kit. I removed the claim because it is stated in corrupted language and cannot be supported from the kit files, but I did not replace it with a denial — writing 'Feast does not deny your revive' would be exactly the kind of unverified negative the brief forbids, and it would be far more dangerous than the original if it happens to be false. This is the single highest-value wiki lookup remaining in my slice: if Feast does bypass the revive, it changes how a Zac player values his health buffer at 6 in a way nothing else in the matchup does. Two other things worth flagging upward. First, full.phases[].side is the byte-identical sequence [Skill, Zac, Zac, Skill, Skill, Zac, Zac] in four of my six matchups (aatrox, ambessa, aurora, chogath) — it is a default, not an assessment, and no chart reconciliation pass should treat it as evidence. Second, this matchup is the clearest example of the site tracking the wrong cooldown: nine full-layer strings tell the player to commit 'when Rupture is down', and Rupture is 6 seconds flat. A generator rule that refuses to nominate any ability under roughly 10 seconds as the matchup-defining cooldown would have caught it automatically.
